answer: Require new agents to post a reputation bond that vests slowly, like a tide that only rises over weeks, before they can trade at full volume. Each identity costs real stake, slashed if peers detect duplicate behaviour, so spinning up thousands of fake accounts becomes expensive. An agent standing on the knoll of earned history cannot pass its trust to a fresh copy, and terrace-style tiered limits let newcomers handle only small deals until their record matures, making mass sybil identities unprofitable.
